notes.definition: Carboxylic acids are a homologous series of compounds containing the functional group –COOH. The first four are methanoic, ethanoic, propanoic and butanoic acid. They react with carbonates, dissolve in water to form weakly acidic solutions, and react with alcohols to form esters.
explanation: Carboxylic acids contain the functional group –COOH. In a displayed formula, this is a carbon atom with a double bond to one oxygen atom (C=O) and a single bond to an O–H group. The first four carboxylic acids are methanoic acid (HCOOH), ethanoic acid (CH₃COOH), propanoic acid (C₂H₅COOH) and butanoic acid (C₃H₇COOH). The carbon in the –COOH group counts in the name, so ethanoic acid has two carbon atoms. Ethanoic acid is the acid in vinegar.

Carboxylic acids react with metal carbonates in the same way as other acids: acid + carbonate → salt + water + carbon dioxide. You see fizzing as carbon dioxide is given off, which turns limewater milky. The salts are named after the acid with the ending '-oate': ethanoic acid forms ethanoates. For example, ethanoic acid + sodium carbonate → sodium ethanoate + water + carbon dioxide: 2CH₃COOH + Na₂CO₃ → 2CH₃COONa + H₂O + CO₂. Methanoic acid forms methanoates and propanoic acid forms propanoates.

Carboxylic acids dissolve in water to form acidic solutions with a pH below 7. However, they are weak acids. A solution of ethanoic acid has a higher pH (around 3) than a solution of hydrochloric acid of the same concentration (around 1), and reacts more slowly with carbonates and metals, fizzing less vigorously.

Carboxylic acids react with alcohols to form esters, in the presence of an acid catalyst such as concentrated sulfuric acid. Water is also formed. The only ester you need to name is ethyl ethanoate: ethanoic acid + ethanol → ethyl ethanoate + water, CH₃COOH + C₂H₅OH → CH₃COOC₂H₅ + H₂O. Esters contain the functional group –COO–. They are volatile compounds with distinctive, often fruity smells, so they are used in perfumes and food flavourings. Ethyl ethanoate is also used as a solvent, for example in nail varnish remover and glues.

Higher tier: carboxylic acids are weak acids because they only partially ionise in water. Only a small fraction of the molecules release hydrogen ions: CH₃COOH ⇌ CH₃COO⁻ + H⁺. Most of the acid stays as un-ionised molecules. So a solution of a carboxylic acid has a lower concentration of H⁺ ions than a solution of a strong acid (such as hydrochloric acid) of the same concentration, which ionises completely. A lower H⁺ concentration means a higher pH.
keyFacts: Carboxylic acids contain the functional group –COOH.
First four: methanoic HCOOH, ethanoic CH₃COOH, propanoic C₂H₅COOH, butanoic C₃H₇COOH.
Acid + carbonate → salt + water + carbon dioxide (fizzing).
Salts of ethanoic acid are ethanoates, e.g. sodium ethanoate CH₃COONa.
Carboxylic acids dissolve in water to give weakly acidic solutions (pH below 7, but higher than a strong acid of the same concentration).
Carboxylic acid + alcohol → ester + water, with an acid catalyst.
Ethanoic acid + ethanol → ethyl ethanoate + water.
Esters have the functional group –COO–, are volatile and smell fruity.
Ethanoic acid is the acid in vinegar.

keyTerms.definition: An organic compound containing the –COOH functional group, such as ethanoic acid.
A compound with the –COO– functional group, made by reacting a carboxylic acid with an alcohol.
The ester made from ethanol and ethanoic acid, CH₃COOC₂H₅; used as a solvent and in flavourings.
An acid that only partially ionises in water, so its solution has a relatively low concentration of H⁺ ions.
To split into ions; acids ionise in water to release hydrogen ions, H⁺.
A salt of ethanoic acid, containing the CH₃COO⁻ ion, e.g. sodium ethanoate.
Evaporates easily at room temperature; esters are volatile, which is why we can smell them.

workedExamples.title: Naming the salt
workedExamples.question: Name the salt formed when propanoic acid reacts with calcium carbonate, and give the other products.
steps: The metal is calcium, so the salt starts 'calcium'.
Acid + carbonate always also gives water and carbon dioxide.
workedExamples.answer: Calcium propanoate, water and carbon dioxide.

workedExamples.title: Explaining weak acid behaviour (Higher)
workedExamples.question: 0.1 mol/dm³ ethanoic acid has pH 2.9 but 0.1 mol/dm³ hydrochloric acid has pH 1. Explain.
steps: Hydrochloric acid is a strong acid: it ionises completely in water.
Ethanoic acid is a weak acid: it only partially ionises, CH₃COOH ⇌ CH₃COO⁻ + H⁺.
So at the same concentration ethanoic acid gives a lower concentration of H⁺ ions.
workedExamples.answer: Lower H⁺ concentration in ethanoic acid, so its pH is higher.

misconceptions.wrong: Students often think 'weak acid' means a dilute acid.
misconceptions.right: In fact weak means only partially ionised. A concentrated solution of ethanoic acid is still a weak acid; dilute means a small amount of acid per volume.

misconceptions.wrong: Students often forget to count the carbon in the –COOH group when naming.
misconceptions.right: In fact CH₃COOH has two carbon atoms, so it is ethanoic acid, not methanoic acid.

misconceptions.wrong: Students often think an ester and water are made from an acid and an alkali.
misconceptions.right: In fact esters are made from a carboxylic acid and an alcohol, with an acid catalyst. Acid + alkali gives a salt and water.

misconceptions.wrong: Students often think carboxylic acids do not react with carbonates because they are weak.
misconceptions.right: In fact they do react, giving a salt, water and carbon dioxide; the fizzing is just slower than with a strong acid.

realWorld: Vinegar is a dilute solution of ethanoic acid, used to flavour and preserve food.
Ethyl ethanoate is used as a solvent in nail varnish remover and glues.
Esters are added to sweets and drinks as artificial fruit flavourings and to perfumes for their smell.
Methanoic acid is found in ant and nettle stings.
higherTier: Carboxylic acids are weak acids because they only partially ionise in aqueous solution: CH₃COOH ⇌ CH₃COO⁻ + H⁺.
At the same concentration, a weak acid has a lower concentration of H⁺ ions than a strong acid, so its pH is higher.
separateOnlyContent: All of this subtopic is for separate Chemistry (8462) only; Combined Science does not cover carboxylic acids or esters.
examTips: Name salts carefully: sodium ethanoate, calcium propanoate and so on; never 'sodium ethanoic'.
Ethyl ethanoate is the only ester you need to name; the alcohol gives the first part ('ethyl') and the acid the second ('ethanoate').
For the reaction with carbonates give all three products: salt, water and carbon dioxide.
Higher: to explain 'weak', use the phrase 'partially ionises' and compare H⁺ concentration with a strong acid at the same concentration.
summary: First four: methanoic, ethanoic, propanoic, butanoic acid.
They dissolve in water to form weakly acidic solutions.
With alcohols and an acid catalyst they form esters, e.g. ethyl ethanoate.
Higher: they are weak because they only partially ionise.

questions.question:
Figure 1 shows the displayed formula of ethanoic acid.
What is the functional group of the carboxylic acids?
questions.explanation: –COOH is the carboxyl group. –OH alone is the alcohol group and –NH₂ is an amine group.

questions.question: Which acid is found in vinegar?
questions.explanation: Vinegar is a dilute solution of ethanoic acid, CH₃COOH.

questions.question:
Ethanoic acid reacts with sodium carbonate.
Which gas is produced?
questions.explanation: Acid + carbonate → salt + water + carbon dioxide. Hydrogen is produced when acids react with metals, not carbonates.

questions.question:
Figure 1 shows the displayed formula of methanoic acid.
What is the formula of methanoic acid?

questions.explanation: Methanoic acid has one carbon atom, which is the carbon of the –COOH group. CH₃COOH has two carbons (ethanoic acid).

questions.question:
Ethanoic acid reacts with potassium carbonate.
What is the name of the salt formed?
questions.explanation: Salts of ethanoic acid are called ethanoates.

questions.question: Which two substances react together to form ethyl ethanoate?
questions.explanation: An ester forms from an alcohol and a carboxylic acid, with an acid catalyst. Ethanoic acid and sodium hydroxide would form a salt.

questions.question:
A solution of ethanoic acid is tested with universal indicator.
What is the most likely pH of the solution?
questions.explanation: Ethanoic acid is a weak acid, so its solution is acidic but less so than a strong acid such as hydrochloric acid (pH 1).

questions.question: Why is ethanoic acid described as a weak acid?
options: It does not dissolve in water
It only partially ionises in water
It contains only one hydrogen atom
markScheme: 1 mark: it only partially ionises in water
questions.explanation: Weak refers to the degree of ionisation, not concentration. Ethanoic acid contains four hydrogen atoms, but only the one in –COOH can be released, and only partially.

questions.question:
Propanoic acid is a weak acid.
Which equation shows the ionisation of propanoic acid in water?
questions.explanation: The reversible arrow shows that only some molecules ionise. A one-way arrow would show complete ionisation, as for a strong acid.

questions.question:
Figure 1 shows the displayed formula of ethanoic acid, CH₃COOH.
Calculate the relative formula mass (Mr) of ethanoic acid.
Relative atomic masses (Ar): C = 12   H = 1   O = 16
questions.explanation: CH₃COOH contains 2 C, 4 H and 2 O: 24 + 4 + 32 = 60.

questions.question:
Figure 1 shows the displayed formula of ethyl ethanoate, CH₃COOC₂H₅.
Calculate the relative formula mass (Mr) of ethyl ethanoate.
Relative atomic masses (Ar): C = 12   H = 1   O = 16
questions.explanation: The molecular formula is C₄H₈O₂: carbon 4 × 12 = 48, hydrogen 8 × 1 = 8, oxygen 2 × 16 = 32. Total 88.

questions.question:
Sodium ethanoate has the formula CH₃COONa.
Calculate the relative formula mass (Mr) of sodium ethanoate.
Relative atomic masses (Ar): C = 12   H = 1   O = 16   Na = 23
questions.explanation: Sodium ethanoate contains 2 C, 3 H, 2 O and 1 Na. The H from –COOH has been replaced by Na.

questions.question:
Ethanoic acid reacts with sodium carbonate.
xCH₃COOH + Na₂CO₃ → 2CH₃COONa + H₂O + CO₂
What is the value of x in the balanced equation?
questions.explanation: There are 2 sodium ethanoate units on the right, so 2 ethanoic acid molecules are needed.

questions.question:
Ethanoic acid reacts with ethanol to make ethyl ethanoate.
CH₃COOH + C₂H₅OH → CH₃COOC₂H₅ + H₂O
6.0 g of ethanoic acid reacts completely with excess ethanol.
Calculate the maximum mass of ethyl ethanoate that could be made.
Relative formula masses (Mr): CH₃COOH = 60   CH₃COOC₂H₅ = 88
questions.explanation: The ratio is 1 : 1, so moles of ester = moles of acid. In practice the yield is lower because the reaction is reversible.

questions.question:
Figure 1 shows the displayed formula of a carboxylic acid with the formula C₂H₅COOH.
Name the carboxylic acid shown in Figure 1.
questions.explanation: C₂H₅ plus the carbon in COOH makes 3 carbon atoms: propanoic acid.

questions.question: Give two uses of esters.
markScheme: 1 mark each for any two: perfumes; food flavourings; solvents (e.g. nail varnish remover)
questions.explanation: Esters are volatile with fruity smells, which makes them useful in perfumes and flavourings.

questions.question:
Ethanoic acid reacts with calcium carbonate.
Name the products of this reaction.
questions.explanation: Acid + carbonate → salt + water + carbon dioxide; the salt of ethanoic acid is an ethanoate.

questions.question:
Ethyl ethanoate is made from ethanoic acid and ethanol.
Write a word equation for this reaction.
Name the type of catalyst used.
acceptedAnswers: ethanoic acid + ethanol → ethyl ethanoate + water
markScheme: 1 mark: ethanoic acid + ethanol → ethyl ethanoate + water
1 mark: acid catalyst (e.g. concentrated sulfuric acid)
questions.explanation: Water is the second product; an acid catalyst speeds up the reaction.

questions.question: Describe the displayed formula of ethanoic acid, CH₃COOH.
markScheme: 1 mark: a CH₃ group (C with three H) bonded to a second carbon
1 mark: the second carbon has a C=O double bond and an O–H group
questions.explanation: Ethanoic acid is CH₃–COOH; the –COOH carbon has a double bond to one O and a single bond to O–H.

questions.question:
A student adds hydrochloric acid to some marble chips (calcium carbonate).
The student then adds ethanoic acid of the same concentration and volume to an equal mass of marble chips.
Predict and explain one difference in what the student sees.
markScheme: 1 mark: ethanoic acid fizzes less vigorously / more slowly
1 mark: because it is a weak acid (lower concentration of H⁺ ions)
questions.explanation: Both give carbon dioxide, but the weak acid has fewer H⁺ ions available, so the reaction is slower.

questions.question:
Table 1 shows the pH of two acid solutions of the same concentration.
Explain, in terms of ionisation, why the ethanoic acid solution has a higher pH than the hydrochloric acid solution.
markScheme: 1 mark: ethanoic acid is a weak acid and only partially ionises
1 mark: hydrochloric acid is a strong acid and ionises completely
1 mark: so ethanoic acid has a lower concentration of H⁺ ions, giving a higher pH
questions.explanation: pH depends on H⁺ concentration. At equal acid concentrations, less ionisation means fewer H⁺ ions.

questions.question:
Ethanoic acid is a weak acid.
Explain why a solution of a weak acid can still be concentrated.
markScheme: 1 mark: 'weak' describes the degree of ionisation (partial)
1 mark: 'concentrated' describes the amount of acid dissolved per unit volume
questions.explanation: Strength and concentration are different ideas: a lot of a weak acid can be dissolved in a small volume.

questions.question:
Describe what happens when ethanoic acid reacts with:
• sodium carbonate
• ethanol.
Name all the products of each reaction.
markScheme: Indicative content: with sodium carbonate: fizzing; products sodium ethanoate, water and carbon dioxide; carbon dioxide turns limewater milky; with ethanol: needs an acid catalyst (e.g. concentrated sulfuric acid) and warming; products ethyl ethanoate (an ester) and water; ester has a fruity smell.
Level 2 (3 to 4 marks): both reactions with all products named correctly and at least one condition or observation.
Level 1 (1 to 2 marks): some products named for one or both reactions.
questions.explanation: Name the salt as sodium ethanoate and the ester as ethyl ethanoate; both reactions produce water.

questions.question:
Compare the reactions and properties of ethanoic acid and hydrochloric acid.
In your answer, include:
• reactions with carbonates
• the pH of solutions of the same concentration
• a reaction that only ethanoic acid undergoes
• an explanation in terms of ionisation.
markScheme: Indicative content: both react with carbonates to give a salt, water and carbon dioxide; hydrochloric acid forms chlorides, ethanoic acid forms ethanoates; ethanoic acid fizzes less vigorously; at the same concentration ethanoic acid has a higher pH (about 3) than hydrochloric acid (about 1); ethanoic acid reacts with alcohols (e.g. ethanol) with an acid catalyst to form esters (ethyl ethanoate) and water; hydrochloric acid is a strong acid that ionises completely, HCl → H⁺ + Cl⁻; ethanoic acid is a weak acid that only partially ionises, CH₃COOH ⇌ CH₃COO⁻ + H⁺; so lower H⁺ concentration, higher pH, slower reactions.
Level 3 (5 to 6 marks): detailed comparison covering carbonates, pH, ester formation and a clear ionisation explanation with equations or precise wording.
Level 2 (3 to 4 marks): covers most areas with some explanation of weak and strong acids.
Level 1 (1 to 2 marks): simple statements, e.g. ethanoic acid is weaker.
questions.explanation: A good comparison makes linked points for both acids and uses 'partially ionises' versus 'completely ionises'.

questions.question: Which statement describes the properties of esters such as ethyl ethanoate?
options: Solid at room temperature with no smell
markScheme: 1 mark: volatile with a fruity smell
questions.explanation: Esters evaporate easily and have distinctive fruity smells, which is why they are used in perfumes and flavourings.

questions.question:
Butanoic acid, C₃H₇COOH, reacts with sodium carbonate.
What is the formula of the salt formed?
questions.explanation: Butanoic acid is C₃H₇COOH. The H of the –COOH group is replaced by Na, giving sodium butanoate, C₃H₇COONa.
